# Scroll

Headers: `winui/ui/scrolling/Scroll.hpp`, `winui/ui/scrolling/ScrollBarOverlay.hpp`. Spec: `winui/ui/scrolling/Scroll.hpp`.

A viewport that scrolls and zooms one child, with overlay scroll bars.

The child is measured without a limit along the scrolling axes ([content_orientation()](#content_orientation)) and drawn clipped and offset. Offsets are in zoomed DIPs, from 0 to [scrollable_width()](#scrollable_width) and [scrollable_height()](#scrollable_height). The wheel scrolls, Ctrl+wheel zooms while [zoom_mode()](#zoom_mode) allows it, the bars drag and step, and with [set_focusable()](#set_focusable) the keys scroll too. [scroll_to()](#scroll_to), [scroll_by()](#scroll_by), [zoom_to()](#zoom_to), [zoom_by()](#zoom_by) and [add_scroll_velocity()](#add_scroll_velocity) move it from code, animated by default. Each returns a correlation id that its completed event reports. The declarative form is [ui::Scroll](#uiscroll).

Example: 
```cpp
auto view = std::make_unique<ui::ScrollControl>();
view->set_height(300.0f);
view->set_zoom_mode(ui::ScrollZoomMode::Enabled);
auto* list = view->set_child(std::make_unique<ui::StackControl>(ui::Orientation::Vertical));
for (int i = 0; i < 100; ++i)
{
    list->add(std::make_unique<ui::TextControl>(std::format("Row {}", i)));
}
view->on_view_changed([v = view.get()] { std::println("at {}", v->vertical_offset()); });
view->on_scroll_completed([](int id) { std::println("scroll {} done", id); });
ui::ScrollControl* observer = view.get();
window.set_content(std::move(view));

observer->scroll_to(0.0f, 500.0f); // animated; lands after the first layout if called before it
```

## `ui::Scroll`

A scrollable, zoomable viewport around one child. Builds a [ui::ScrollControl](#uiscrollcontrol). The modes and bar visibilities can be bound.

Give it a bounded size, such as a [`height`](../conventions.md#common-fields-on-every-spec), a star grid row or a window, or it grows to its content and has nothing to scroll. [`horizontal_offset`](#uiscroll-horizontal_offset), [`vertical_offset`](#uiscroll-vertical_offset) and [`zoom_factor`](#uiscroll-zoom_factor) bind two-way: the user's scrolling writes them, and writing them moves the view at once. Animated scrolling goes through [`.control`](#uiscroll-control): scroll_to(), scroll_by(), zoom_to().

Example: 
```cpp
const std::string       long_text = "A text much taller than the window...";
ui::Property<float>     position{0.0f};
ui::Control<ui::Scroll> scroller;

window.set_content(ui::VerticalStack{.content = {
    ui::Button{.text = "Back to top", .on_click = [&] { scroller->scroll_to(0.0f, 0.0f); }},
    ui::Text{.text = ui::bind(position, [](float y) { return std::format("{:.0f} DIPs down", y); })},
    ui::Scroll{
        .vertical_offset = position, // follows the user's scrolling; writing it jumps
        .zoom_mode       = ui::ScrollZoomMode::Enabled,
        .height          = 400.0f,
        .control         = scroller,
        .content         = ui::Text{.text = long_text, .wrapping = ui::TextWrapping::Wrap},
    },
}});
```

## `ui::ScrollControl`

Derives from `ui::Element`, `ui::ScrollProvider`.

A viewport that scrolls and zooms one child, with overlay scroll bars.

The child is measured without a limit along the scrolling axes ([content_orientation()](#content_orientation)) and drawn clipped and offset. Offsets are in zoomed DIPs, from 0 to [scrollable_width()](#scrollable_width) and [scrollable_height()](#scrollable_height). The wheel scrolls, Ctrl+wheel zooms while [zoom_mode()](#zoom_mode) allows it, the bars drag and step, and with [set_focusable()](#set_focusable) the keys scroll too. [scroll_to()](#scroll_to), [scroll_by()](#scroll_by), [zoom_to()](#zoom_to), [zoom_by()](#zoom_by) and [add_scroll_velocity()](#add_scroll_velocity) move it from code, animated by default. Each returns a correlation id that its completed event reports. The declarative form is [ui::Scroll](#uiscroll).

Example: 
```cpp

for (int i = 0; i < 100; ++i)

    list->add(std::make_unique<ui::TextControl>(std::format("Row {}", i)));
```

### pan_on_drag

```cpp
bool pan_on_drag() const
```

Whether dragging the content with the left button moves the view, as a hand tool does. A pen or a finger counts as the left button. Off by default. Only a press that nothing inside handles starts a pan, so the content's buttons and boxes keep their clicks, and only the axes the user may scroll ([computed_horizontal_scroll_mode()](#computed_horizontal_scroll_mode), [computed_vertical_scroll_mode()](#computed_vertical_scroll_mode)) move. While there is something to pan, the pointer shows the move cursor over the content.

### set_pan_on_drag

```cpp
void set_pan_on_drag(bool pan)
```

Takes effect on the next press. Turning it off during a drag lets the drag finish.

### scroll_to

```cpp
int scroll_to(float horizontal_offset, float vertical_offset, ScrollOptions options = {})
```

Moves the view to the given offsets, in zoomed DIPs clamped to the scrollable range, animated unless `options` say otherwise. Stops any running animation or inertia and completes its request.

Each of these calls returns the request's correlation id, which the matching completed event reports. A request made before the first layout waits until then, so a view set up right after it is built lands against the real viewport.

### scroll_by

```cpp
int scroll_by(float horizontal_delta, float vertical_delta, ScrollOptions options = {})
```

[scroll_to()](#scroll_to) the current offsets plus the deltas.

### add_scroll_velocity

```cpp
int add_scroll_velocity(Point offsets_velocity, std::optional<Point> inertia_decay_rate = std::nullopt)
```

Starts an inertial coast at `offsets_velocity` DIPs per second, or adds to the velocity of one already coasting. `inertia_decay_rate` is per axis, in [0, 1]. nullopt is 0.95, and 0 keeps a constant speed.

### zoom_to

```cpp
int zoom_to(float zoom_factor, std::optional<Point> center_point = std::nullopt, ScrollZoomOptions options = {})
```

Changes the zoom factor, clamped to the zoom range, about [`center_point`](../tree/element.md#center_point), which is relative to the viewport. nullopt is the viewport's center.

### zoom_by

```cpp
int zoom_by(float zoom_factor_delta, std::optional<Point> center_point = std::nullopt, ScrollZoomOptions options = {})
```

[zoom_to()](#zoom_to) the current factor plus `zoom_factor_delta`.

```cpp
bool covers_children_at(Point p) const override
```

Whether a part of this element drawn over its children is at `p` (a scroll bar over the content), so the element is hit there instead of a child. Default: false.

### tick_override

```cpp
void tick_override(Duration delta) override
```

Advances the scroll bars' fades, any scroll or zoom animation and any inertia, then ticks the content.

### enabled_changed

```cpp
void enabled_changed() override
```

[is_enabled()](../tree/element.md#is_enabled) flipped, through [set_enabled()](../tree/element.md#set_enabled) here or on an ancestor, or a move to another parent. Drop any press or hover state. The element is redrawn either way. No-op by default.

### key_override

```cpp
bool key_override(const KeyEvent& e) override
```

While focused, the arrow keys scroll 15 % of the viewport, Page Up and Page Down a whole viewport, and Home and End go to either end.

### focus_changed

```cpp
void focus_changed(bool focused) override
```

Called by [Window](../tree/window.md) as focus moves; redraws.

## class ScrollBarOverlay

The overlay scroll bar a scrolling [Element](../tree/element.md) paints over its own viewport. It is a part of its owner, not an [Element](../tree/element.md) itself.

It holds only interaction and animation state. The owner passes the viewport, the content length and the current offset into every call, and applies the offset [handle_pointer()](#handle_pointer) hands back. At rest it is a thin thumb flush with the edge. Hovered or dragged, it widens and shows a track and two step buttons. After 2 s without activity it fades away. [Scroll](#uiscroll) and VirtualList use it, and a custom scroller uses it the same way.

Example: 
```cpp
class Scroller final : public ui::Element
{
public:
    ui::Size measure_override(ui::Size available, const ui::MeasureContext&) const override
    {
        return available;
    }
    bool pointer_override(const ui::PointerEvent& e) override
    {
        float offset = offset_;
        if (bar_.handle_pointer(e, bounds(), content_height_, offset))
        {
            offset_ = offset; // clamp and re-arrange here
            mark_dirty(ui::DirtyFlags::Visual);
            return true; // claimed: do not forward to the content
        }
        return false; // ... or forward to the content ...
    }
    void tick_override(ui::Duration delta) override
    {
        if (bar_.update(delta))
        {
            mark_dirty(ui::DirtyFlags::Visual);
        }
        if (const std::optional<ui::Duration> wait = bar_.fade_wait())
        {
            request_tick_in(*wait); // wake once for the fade
        }
    }
    void render_override(ui::Renderer& renderer, const ui::RenderContext& context) const override
    {
        // ... render the clipped content first ...
        bar_.render(renderer, theme, bounds(), content_height_, offset_);
    }

private:
    ui::ScrollBarOverlay bar_{ui::Orientation::Vertical};
    float                   offset_         = 0.0f;
    float                   content_height_ = 1000.0f;
};
```

### ScrollBarOverlay

```cpp
ScrollBarOverlay(Orientation orientation = Orientation::Vertical)
```

A bar for one axis, collapsed and idle.

### orientation

```cpp
Orientation orientation() const
```

The axis given at construction.

### scrollable

```cpp
bool scrollable(const Rect& viewport, float content_length) const
```

Whether `content_length` (DIPs along this bar's axis) exceeds the viewport along it.

### always_visible

```cpp
bool always_visible() const
```

ScrollBarVisibility::Visible: draw the bar even with nothing to scroll. Its thumb then fills the track, and it takes no input. Off by default, which is Auto.

### set_always_visible

```cpp
void set_always_visible(bool always)
```

The owner redraws. This class marks nothing dirty.

### apply_theme

```cpp
void apply_theme(const Theme& theme) const
```

Takes the theme's kind of bar: this overlay, or a permanent bar, which takes room of its own at full thickness and never fades. The owner calls it in measure, where it has the theme, before it lays its content out.

### gutter

```cpp
float gutter() const
```

The room the bar takes from its scroller's viewport while it shows, in DIPs: the era bar's thickness, or 0 for the overlay, which draws over the content.

### band_bounds

```cpp
Rect band_bounds(const Rect& viewport) const
```

The area that takes the bar's input: the rightmost, full-height, 12-DIP slice of the viewport, whether the bar is expanded or not. A click or hover must land in it to reach the bar. It spans the step buttons and the thumb and track between them. For a horizontal bar, it is the bottom row.

### up_button_bounds

```cpp
Rect up_button_bounds(const Rect& viewport) const
```

The up (top) step button, or the left one for a horizontal bar: a 12-DIP square at that end of the band, which scrolls back a small step. Both step buttons always take their space, however far the expand animation is, and the thumb's track stops short of them. Only their drawing fades with the animation.

### down_button_bounds

```cpp
Rect down_button_bounds(const Rect& viewport) const
```

The down (bottom) step button, or the right one for a horizontal bar; see [up_button_bounds()](#up_button_bounds).

### thumb_bounds

```cpp
Rect thumb_bounds(const Rect& viewport, float content_length, float offset) const
```

Where the thumb is drawn for `offset`, the DIPs scrolled into `content_length`. Its length is the viewport's share of the track between the step buttons, at least 30 DIPs, at the thickness the animation has reached.

### expanded

```cpp
bool expanded() const
```

True while hovered or dragging: the expanded look (thicker thumb, visible track) instead of the collapsed one (thin thumb, no track).

### dragging

```cpp
bool dragging() const
```

True while the thumb is being dragged.

### handle_pointer

```cpp
bool handle_pointer(const PointerEvent& e, const Rect& viewport, float content_length, float& offset)
```

The owner passes every pointer event except wheel turns here first. Returns true if the bar took the event, and the owner must then not forward it to its content. When it returns true and `offset` differs from what the owner passed in, the owner applies it the way it applies a wheel turn, through its own offset setter, which clamps and arranges again.

### update

```cpp
bool update(Duration delta)
```

Advances the expand and collapse animation by `delta`. Call it once per frame from the owner's tick_override(). Returns true while an animation is still running. The owner then marks itself visually dirty so [render()](#render) is called again.

### fade_wait

```cpp
std::optional<Duration> fade_wait() const
```

How long until the bar starts to fade by itself. Set while it shows and waits out its 2 s without activity, and empty while hovered, dragged, fading or faded. The owner passes it to [Element::request_tick_in()](../tree/element.md#request_tick_in) from tick_override(), so an otherwise idle window wakes once for the fade.

### notify_activity

```cpp
void notify_activity()
```

Restarts the 2 s idle clock after which the bar fades, for activity [handle_pointer()](#handle_pointer) can't see, such as a wheel turn the owner scrolled with, whether or not the pointer is over the band. [Scroll](#uiscroll) and VirtualList call it from their wheel handling. Hovering and dragging keep the clock reset by themselves.

### render

```cpp
void render(Renderer& renderer, const Theme& theme, const Rect& viewport, float content_length, float offset) const
```

Draws nothing when !is_scrollable(viewport, content_length). Call it after the owner has drawn its clipped content. The bar draws on top, unclipped.

### is_scrollable

```cpp
static bool is_scrollable(const Rect& viewport, float content_length)
```

Whether there is anything to scroll at all, which decides whether the bar draws and takes input. This static form checks the vertical axis, and [scrollable()](#scrollable) below checks this bar's own axis.

## struct ScrollOptions

How [ScrollControl::scroll_to()](#scroll_to) and scroll_by() move. Snap points are not supported.

Example: 
```cpp
ui::Control<ui::Scroll> view; // a Scroll's .control

// Back to the top at once, no animation.
view->scroll_to(0.0f, 0.0f, {.animation_mode = ui::ScrollAnimationMode::Disabled});
```

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `animation_mode` | `ScrollAnimationMode` | `ScrollAnimationMode::Auto` | Whether the scroll animates. Auto animates. |

## struct ScrollZoomOptions

How [ScrollControl::zoom_to()](#zoom_to) and zoom_by() change the zoom.

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `animation_mode` | `ScrollAnimationMode` | `ScrollAnimationMode::Auto` | Whether the zoom animates. Auto animates. |

## struct KeyFrameEasing

How a key frame eases in from the one before it: a cubic Bézier curve, or a step easing when [`steps`](#steps) is positive. A step easing jumps in [`steps`](#steps) equal steps, the last of them at the key frame itself.

### curve

```cpp
CubicBezier curve = easing::ControlFastOutSlowIn
```

The curve, used while [`steps`](#steps) is 0. Fluent's fast-out-slow-in by default.

### steps

```cpp
int steps = 0
```

A positive count makes this a step easing instead of [`curve`](#curve).

### evaluate

```cpp
float evaluate(double x) const
```

The eased progress (0..1) at linear progress `x` (0..1) between the two key frames.

## struct ScrollKeyFrame

One key frame of a scroll animation: at [`progress`](#struct-scrollkeyframe), 0 to 1 of the duration, the view is at [`offsets`](#struct-scrollkeyframe). The offsets are horizontal and vertical, in zoomed DIPs, and are clamped to the scrollable range as the animation plays.

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `progress` | `float` | `1.0f` | Where in the animation the frame sits, 0..1 of the duration. |
| `offsets` | `Point` |  | The (horizontal, vertical) offsets the view reaches at [`progress`](#struct-scrollkeyframe). |
| `easing` | `KeyFrameEasing` |  | How the view eases in from the previous key frame. |

## struct ScrollAnimation

The key-frame animation a [Scroll](#uiscroll) builds for an animated scroll. By default it is one key frame at 1.0 on the target, over a duration that depends on the distance. The start at progress 0 is implicit. [Key](../core/namespace-ui.md#key) frames play in `progress` order.

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `duration` | `Duration` |  | The whole animation's length. |
| `key_frames` | `std::vector<ScrollKeyFrame>` |  | The frames after the implicit start. |

## struct ScrollAnimationStarting

The arguments of [ScrollControl::on_scroll_animation_starting()](#on_scroll_animation_starting). The handler may edit or replace [`animation`](#struct-scrollanimationstarting). [`start_position`](#struct-scrollanimationstarting) and [`end_position`](#struct-scrollanimationstarting) are the offsets the view moves between.

Example: 
```cpp
ui::Control<ui::Scroll> view; // a Scroll's .control
view->on_scroll_animation_starting([](ui::ScrollAnimationStarting& args) {
    args.animation.duration   = 600ms; // slower than the distance-based default
    args.animation.key_frames = {
        {.progress = 0.5f, .offsets = args.start_position},  // hold, then
        {.progress = 1.0f, .offsets = args.end_position},    // move
    };
});
```

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `animation` | `ScrollAnimation` |  | The animation about to play. The handler may change it. |
| `start_position` | `Point` |  | The offsets the view starts from. |
| `end_position` | `Point` |  | The offsets the request targets. |
| `correlation_id` | `int` | `0` | The id scroll_to()/scroll_by() returned for this request. |

## struct ZoomKeyFrame

One key frame of a zoom animation. It carries a zoom factor, applied about the animation's `center_point`.

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `progress` | `float` | `1.0f` | Where in the animation the frame sits, 0..1 of the duration. |
| `zoom_factor` | `float` | `1.0f` | The zoom factor reached at [`progress`](#struct-zoomkeyframe). |
| `easing` | `KeyFrameEasing` |  | How the zoom eases in from the previous key frame. |

## struct ZoomAnimation

The key-frame animation a [Scroll](#uiscroll) builds for an animated zoom. By default it is one key frame at 1.0 on the target factor, over 250 ms per whole zoom step, kept within 50 to 1000 ms.

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `duration` | `Duration` |  | The whole animation's length. |
| `key_frames` | `std::vector<ZoomKeyFrame>` |  | The frames after the implicit start, in `progress` order. |

## struct ZoomAnimationStarting

The arguments of [ScrollControl::on_zoom_animation_starting()](#on_zoom_animation_starting). The handler may edit or replace [`animation`](#struct-zoomanimationstarting), as in [ScrollAnimationStarting](#struct-scrollanimationstarting).

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `animation` | `ZoomAnimation` |  | The animation about to play. The handler may change it. |
| `start_zoom_factor` | `float` | `1.0f` | The zoom factor the view starts from. |
| `end_zoom_factor` | `float` | `1.0f` | The zoom factor the request targets. |
| `center_point` | `Point` |  | The point kept still while zooming, in DIPs relative to the viewport. |
| `correlation_id` | `int` | `0` | The id zoom_to()/zoom_by() returned for this request. |

## Enumerations

### ScrollContentOrientation

```cpp
enum class ScrollContentOrientation
```

Which axes a [Scroll](#uiscroll)'s content is free to grow along.

| Value | |
| --- | --- |
| `Vertical` | Width fixed to the viewport, height free (the default). |
| `Horizontal` | Height fixed to the viewport, width free. |
| `None` | Both fixed: the content fits the viewport, and zooming shows more. |
| `Both` | Both free. |

### ScrollMode

```cpp
enum class ScrollMode
```

Whether the user can scroll along an axis.

| Value | |
| --- | --- |
| `Enabled` | The wheel, the scroll bar and the keys scroll this axis. |
| `Disabled` | User input leaves this axis alone. scroll_to() and the other calls still move it. |
| `Auto` | Enabled while the axis has something to scroll, or while zooming is enabled. |

### ScrollZoomMode

```cpp
enum class ScrollZoomMode
```

Whether the user can zoom (Ctrl+wheel).

| Value | |
| --- | --- |
| `Enabled` | Ctrl+wheel zooms, 10 % a notch. |
| `Disabled` | The default. zoom_to() and zoom_by() still work. |

### ScrollChainMode

```cpp
enum class ScrollChainMode
```

Whether a wheel turn this view cannot use, because it is already at the end the turn points toward, goes on to the scroller around it. Auto and Always differ only for touch input, which the library does not handle, so both pass the turn on. Never keeps the turn, and the page behind does not move.

| Value | |
| --- | --- |
| `Auto` | Pass the turn on (the default). |
| `Always` | Pass the turn on, the same as Auto without touch. |
| `Never` | Keep the turn. |

### ScrollBarVisibility

```cpp
enum class ScrollBarVisibility
```

When a scroll bar shows.

| Value | |
| --- | --- |
| `Auto` | Shown while its axis is scrollable and its scroll mode enabled. |
| `Visible` | Always shown. |
| `Hidden` | Never shown. |

### ScrollAnimationMode

```cpp
enum class ScrollAnimationMode
```

Whether a programmatic view change animates.

| Value | |
| --- | --- |
| `Disabled` | Jump straight to the target. |
| `Enabled` | Animate over a duration that depends on the distance. |
| `Auto` | Always animates. The system animation setting is not checked. |

### ScrollInteractionState

```cpp
enum class ScrollInteractionState
```

What is moving the view right now ([ScrollControl::state()](#state)).

| Value | |
| --- | --- |
| `Idle` | Nothing. |
| `Interaction` | A scroll bar thumb is being dragged. |
| `Inertia` | An add_scroll_velocity() is coasting. |
| `Animating` | A scroll_to(), scroll_by(), zoom_to() or zoom_by() is animating. |
